title: A hundred years since she was born, twenty-two before anyone can look
client: The estate of a painter who died in 1998, administered by her niece and a solicitor. The niece has run it for twenty-six years, has turned down every request, and describes the job as keeping a promise rather than managing an asset. The solicitor is here because the estate has been sued once.
event: She was born in 1926 and would have been a hundred this year. Her will directs that no reproduction of any work be made or licensed for fifty years from her death, which is to say until 2048. Eleven canvases exist. Four are in institutions who agreed to the condition to get them and have honoured it; seven are in the house she died in, in a room the niece opens twice a year to check the humidity. Nobody under fifty has seen any of them.
when: The centenary of her birth falls on 19 November. The embargo lifts in 2048.
where: The village she worked in for thirty years, which has a hall, a shop and a bus twice a day.
function: Mark the centenary in the village, where about two hundred people knew her or knew of her, without breaching the embargo. It has worked if somebody who never knew she existed comes away wanting to see the work and understanding that they cannot, and that this was her decision. It has not worked if they come away thinking the estate is hoarding.
audience: The village, which is elderly and which mostly remembers her as somebody who did not talk about her work. Perhaps thirty people who will travel for it, including two academics who have written about her without ever having seen a canvas. Her great-nephews, who are nineteen and twenty-two and have been told they will not see them either.
production: The niece will pay a local firm that does signage and vehicle livery. One process, whatever they normally run, and they have a fortnight of capacity in October.
quantity: Twenty, for the hall and the shop and the bus shelter, and one to keep.
mustAppear: how many works exist, eleven canvases
the date of the centenary, 19 November
budget: Eight hundred pounds, which the niece is paying herself and has said twice is not a lot.
timeline: By the end of October, so it is up for three weeks before the 19th.
clientWantThatHurtsTheWork: The solicitor requires that nothing be made which could be argued to be a derivation of any specific work, and reads that broadly. He has said that a shape resembling a composition he has never seen would still be a problem, because the estate cannot afford to test it.

The niece wants it made unmistakable that the embargo was the artist's own instruction and not the family's. She has been accused of it for twenty-six years and this is the first public thing the estate has ever commissioned.
Her name, her dates, and the words 'by direction of the artist' are to appear together, at a size where nobody can miss them.
The estate will not release the one photograph that exists of her, taken in 1961, on the grounds that she disliked it. It is the only image of her anywhere.
clientFear: That it reads as an advertisement for something withheld, which would bring exactly the attention the will was written to prevent, and which would put the seven canvases in a house with one lock on it in the minds of people the niece would rather not have thinking about them.
stakes: A promise made to a dying woman by a nineteen-year-old, kept for twenty-six years, with twenty-two still to run. There is no second centenary and the niece is seventy-one. If this makes the estate look secretive rather than faithful, the pressure to break the embargo starts now rather than in 2048.

hard_constraints.why: The centenary is the occasion and the year is the whole of it. Without a date this is a notice about a rule rather than a mark of a hundred years.
A withholding with an end date is a decision somebody made. Without the year it is a refusal, and a refusal is what the family has been accused of for twenty-six years.
The number is the only fact about the work that the embargo permits. It establishes that there is something specific and finite being withheld rather than a reputation being managed.

notes: The niece has a letter from the artist explaining the fifty years. She has never shown it to anyone and has not said whether it may be quoted.
